clue.text: Unusually 21, as it happens

indicators.note: done unusually, the letters of the answer to 21 down come out in a fresh order

parts.note: the answer to 21 down, which is VILE

explanation.surface: Something oddly disgusting is going on right now.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 21 down; its four letters, rearranged, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast that goes out as events happen is described as live, in real time rather than recorded.

clue.text: Tolerance of commonplace remark? Not the first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for a trite remark is left off

parts.note: a platitude is a dull, overused saying

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether putting up with a cliché counts as tolerance, then adds a caveat.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means freedom of action or scope allowed, the leeway that tolerance grants.

clue.text: Spite of archdeacon initially over Mass

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', shortened in writing to Ven. before the name
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A church official's malice was directed against the Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: An Anglican archdeacon carries the title the Venerable, written Ven. at the start of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in the figurative sense is bitter malice or spitefulness in speech or manner.

clue.text: Parent's fur just about acceptable

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father, plus the possessive 's
sable is the prized dark fur of a small marten

explanation.surface: Dad's old fur coat will just about do.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means adequate or tolerable, good enough but no better.

clue.text: Perfect regularity of request for dessert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a state of complete neatness and orderliness
second meaning, read literally: ordering an apple pie for pudding

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally the second time, as a diner's order for a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie order is an idiom for everything being perfectly tidy and arranged.

clue.text: Without excess: in this way, live right

parts.note: so can mean thus, in this manner
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Advice on living the right way: moderately, without indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober means moderate and restrained, especially not drinking too much.

clue.text: One part of Ireland supports Ring composer

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell, and a ring can be a bell's call
I is the Roman numeral for one
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish backer funds a performance of Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring composer' suggests Wagner and his Ring cycle, but Ring is a separate piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini was an Italian opera composer, writer of Norma.

clue.text: Wickedness when 25 is ripped up

indicators.note: a ripped-up item is torn apart, so the letters of the answer to 25 across are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, which is VEIL

explanation.surface: Tearing a bridal veil apart would be an act of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is moral badness or wrongdoing, a straight synonym for sin and depravity.

clue.text: Water-heater bloke heard

indicators.note: what is heard is the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man or bloke

explanation.surface: Someone heard the man who services the boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a geyser is a gas water heater, and it is pronounced like geezer, slang for a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser in Britain is a domestic gas appliance that heats water as it runs.

clue.text: Show strain, present for example in court

parts.note: the present is an example of a grammatical tense
a defendant who is up is appearing before the court

explanation.surface: A witness in court shows strain while giving evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To tense up is to become stiff and anxious, visibly showing stress.

clue.text: North European taking one Indian dish

parts.note: a Balt is a person from the Baltic states
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Latvian visitor chooses a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a wok-like metal bowl, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Runners' individual results in the paper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the finishing ... recorded for each runner
second meaning: The ... newspaper, which publishes this puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as race results printed in a newspaper; 'the paper' is also this crossword's own newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Race results are given as times, and The Times is the newspaper that prints the puzzle.

clue.text: Insect has hair, not its own, on part of head

indicators.note: in an across entry, a piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the ear is on the side of the head
a wig is false hair worn on the head

explanation.surface: A description of someone with a wig perched near their ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The earwig is a small insect with pincers at the rear, once thought to creep into ears.

clue.text: Attending class, a learner relaxed

parts.note: to be in a place is to attend it
a form is a school class in Britain
taken as written
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A student joins a lesson and finds it laid-back.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a school year group or class in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual and relaxed, not following official rules or ceremony.

clue.text: Resolution's extremely decisive conclusion

indicators.note: taking a word to its extremes means using only its first and last letters

parts.note: the word decisive, of which only the two end letters are used
termination is an ending or conclusion

explanation.surface: A firm decision brought matters to a decisive end.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution and determination both mean firmness of purpose in pursuing a goal.

clue.text: Plays idly, taking first of these firearms

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the word these, whose opening letter is taken
rifles are long-barrelled guns

explanation.surface: Someone toys carelessly with a gun collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle is to treat something lightly or toy with it, so trifles means plays idly.

clue.text: Allure of court case

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a hearing in a higher court to overturn a decision

explanation.definitionFit: Appeal means attractiveness, and also an application to a higher court to review a verdict.

clue.text: Mafia scowlingly covering up debacle

indicators.note: the words cover up the answer, holding it within their letters

parts.note: the two words run together, and the answer sits across the join between them

explanation.surface: A gangster scowls while concealing a botched job.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a complete and humiliating failure, the same as a debacle.

clue.text: Disdainfully ignore small growth on foot

parts.note: a corn is a hard patch of thickened skin on the foot

explanation.surface: Someone sniffily dismisses a little bunion.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn is to reject or dismiss with contempt.

clue.text: Breathe hard, needing oxygen for stage show

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath

explanation.surface: A breathless performer needs an oxygen mask during the show.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas family stage show with slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: Panto is short for pantomime, a comic theatrical entertainment.

clue.text: Sister's name sure to be changed

indicators.note: letters that are to be changed are rearranged

parts.note: the word sure, whose four letters are rearranged after the N

explanation.surface: A nun's name is certain to change when she takes vows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' looks like a nun, but in Britain a sister is a senior nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sister is the British title for a senior nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Disgusting sort of 7

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant, so the letters of the answer to 7 down are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, which is EVIL

explanation.surface: A repulsive kind of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Vile means foul, repulsive or morally base.

clue.text: One good toilet in blockhouse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A single decent lavatory in a fortified bunker.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped house made of snow blocks, cryptically a 'block house'.

clue.text: Mausoleum site shown in indistinct map

indicators.note: one piece is shown inside another

parts.note: dim means faint or unclear
Agra in India is the site of the Taj Mahal mausoleum

explanation.surface: A tomb's location is marked on a faded map.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple drawing showing layout, as a map does.

clue.text: Tragic scene of wickedness in European legends

indicators.note: the word for wickedness goes in the other pieces

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional stories
sin is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Old European tales full of tragic wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the Danish castle where Shakespeare's tragedy Hamlet is set.

clue.text: Cover up 1ac broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters of the answer to 1 across are scattered and reset

parts.note: the answer to 1 across, which is LIVE

explanation.surface: Someone hides a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' sits naturally with live television, but here it means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: To veil something is to conceal or cover it.
